action: I thank Beabella for the bread and ask her who the figure in miner's grey was, and where they went so fast.

action: I stay flat behind the peat-mound and hold still, waiting him out rather than moving and risking more noise.
note: no roll requested this turn; Costtore gave up searching, dismissed the noise as a bird/wind, walked back to camp; oilcloth bundle remains buried at seep-line, camp now stirring/cookfire lit; DM prose streamed unusually slowly this turn (long word-by-word render)

action: With Costtore gone, I dig up the oilcloth bundle at the seep-line to see what he buried and what the stamped token is.
note: no roll requested; found Color-Miners debt/membership token + a pinch of unnamed shifting pigment matching the incense-smell from opening; Costtore is hiding stolen impossible pigment from the Color-Miners themselves, frightened; strong worldbuilding hook planted; re-buried it and camp is now fully awake

action: I head back into camp like nothing happened, find a place to sit near the cookfire, and eat Beabella's bread while I watch the camp wake up properly.
note: no roll; turns out I actually kept the bundle (waxed weight against my ribs) rather than reburying - good tension building; Costtore now realizing his stash is missing, visibly afraid; Beabella watching camp like waiting for someone specific

action: I go sit next to Costtore, quiet, and murmur that I found something of his by the water, and that we should talk somewhere private before anyone else notices he's missing it.
note: no roll; excellent tense dialogue beat - Costtore nearly bolted/swung, chose to negotiate, proposed meeting at drying-shed past the tailings before midmorning; DM prose strong throughout this whole thread

action: I wait a few minutes so it doesn't look connected, then follow him toward the drying-shed, staying wary in case this is a trap rather than a negotiation.
note: no roll requested despite tense setup; DM confirmed no ambush (no shapes in the reeds); Costtore waiting inside, hands empty, genuinely just scared and wanting to talk privately

action: I push inside, keeping the door in view, and tell him plainly: I am not here to rob you or turn you in. I want to know what the Color-Miners are, and why a pinch of powder scared you enough to bury it before dawn.
note: long response (170s) but paid off huge - major exposition: Color-Miners run debt bondage sending workers into Strange places to mine impossible colors; the pigment CHANGES people who handle it too long (body-snatcher horror), camp already has infiltrators wearing Miners colors; Costtore buried his pinch to avoid being Changed in his sleep; strong dark hook, well above average narrative quality this session

action: Who in this camp do you think is already Changed? And what happens to the ones who stop being themselves - where do they go?
note: no roll; strong horror payoff - Halvar is fully Changed but indistinguishable from outside (body-snatcher confirmed), Beabella suspected but uncertain, ones who ask too loud stop asking (implied disappearance/violence); bell tolls, Costtore flinches - good tension beat to close scene

action: We should go before we're missed, I say, and hand him back the token, but keep the powder. I offer to hold onto the powder for safety and to be found if he needs help. Then I head back toward camp.
note: no roll; excellent scene closer - Costtore relieved/hopeful, hints others are counting faces too (allies against the Changed); Manfred now literally carries plot-critical item + faction knowledge; very well-written prose throughout this whole opening arc

action: Back in camp, I quietly watch Beabella at the cookfire for a while, comparing what I know about the Changed against her behavior before deciding whether to trust her.
